market_summary: Markets are jittery after Nvidia founder Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation amid a personal scandal wiped $450B off its market cap and triggered a wave of analyst downgrades, dragging US indices and tech-heavy benchmarks lower alongside rising Treasury yields (~5.1%) and Iran-related geopolitical risk. In Singapore, bank earnings diverged sharply - OCBC beat on record profit while DBS and UOB missed on NIM compression - and Singtel rallied on raised FY2027 guidance even as SIA's profit nearly halved on surging fuel costs despite record revenue. Overall risk sentiment is cautious heading into NVDA's Nov 17 earnings and US PPI data, with elevated volatility in event-driven names.

picks.thesis: CEO scandal has triggered a confidence crisis: nine sell-side downgrades hit in a single day (Nov 12), stock is down 4.3% on the day and nearly 25% over the month on 4.5x normal volume. Leadership vacuum (interim CFO-CEO) plus an earnings report in 4 days creates a high-risk window for further downside before the dust settles.
picks.news: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on 2026-11-12 after reports of an extramarital affair involving an alleged Chinese spy; CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO. Nine analysts cut ratings/targets the same day (Melius, Craig-Hallum, StoneX, William Blair, Keybanc, Bernstein, Evercore, Oppenheimer, Baird).
picks.risks: Stock is already down ~30% from 52-week highs and extremely oversold; a stabilizing management statement, reassurance from major customers (Singtel already said deliveries are unaffected), or a strong Nov 17 earnings beat could spark a sharp short-covering rally.

picks.thesis: Singtel raised FY2027 EBIT guidance to mid-to-high single digits on the back of 10% H1 underlying profit growth, driven by NCS, Digital InfraCo and Optus. Management also explicitly confirmed no disruption to AI chip deliveries despite the Nvidia CEO shakeup, removing a key overhang. Analyst sentiment is overwhelmingly positive (13 buy/2 hold out of 16) with ~28% implied upside to consensus target.
picks.news: Singtel H1 underlying profit +10% to S$1.49B and raised FY2027 guidance (2026-11-13); separately confirmed Nvidia CEO exit has not hit AI chip deliveries (2026-11-13).
picks.risks: Reported net profit actually fell 55% due to non-repeat of divestment gains, which could be misread negatively; stock already saw elevated volume (3.3x normal) on earnings day which could mean the reaction is already priced in, and broader market weakness could cap gains.

picks.thesis: SIA's H1 profit plunged 44% as jet fuel costs surged 86.7% amid Middle East conflict, yet the stock is still up 9.5% over the past month and trades above both its 50- and 200-day moving averages. Analyst sentiment is weak (only 1 buy vs 10 hold/3 sell) with consensus target implying slightly negative upside, suggesting the share price has run ahead of deteriorating fundamentals.
picks.news: SIA reported record H1 revenue of S$11.3B but net profit fell 44% to S$134M as fuel bill rose 56% to S$4B on Middle East-driven price spikes (2026-11-11).
picks.risks: Fuel prices could ease if Middle East tensions de-escalate, and strong passenger volume growth (+5% to 21.8M) shows demand resilience that could support the stock despite margin pressure.

picks.thesis: UOB missed Q3 estimates on continued net interest margin compression from rising deposit costs, and unlike DBS/OCBC it trades below its 200-day moving average (-4.6%) signaling a weaker longer-term trend. Analyst sentiment is the most lukewarm of the three banks (5 buy/9 hold/2 sell) and the stock is down 8%+ over both 1-month and 3-month windows.
picks.news: UOB Q3 2026 profit missed expectations amid NIM compression from rising deposit costs and elevated funding expenses (2026-11-04); shares slid alongside DBS after weak 3Q results (2026-11-09).
picks.risks: Banking sector could re-rate broadly if rate-cut expectations shift, or if NIM pressure proves transitory; being the laggard also means it could see mean-reversion buying if sentiment stabilizes.

picks.thesis: OCBC was the only major Singapore bank to beat Q3 estimates, posting 3% YoY profit growth to a record 9-month net profit of S$6.24B, in contrast to DBS and UOB misses on NIM pressure. This relative outperformance plus still-reasonable valuation (7.1% implied upside, trading above its 200-day MA) makes it the preferred pick within the beaten-down SG banking sector.
picks.news: OCBC Q3 2026 net profit rose 3% YoY to S$2.04B, beating forecasts, with 9-month profit at a record S$6.24B, up 10% YoY (2026-11-06).
picks.risks: Sector-wide pressure on margins could still weigh on OCBC in coming quarters, and the stock is down 9.6% over 3 months and 11.6% off its 52-week high, showing it isn't immune to the broader bank sell-off.

picks.thesis: Nasdaq-100 is heavily weighted toward mega-cap tech including Nvidia, and faces headwinds from the Nvidia leadership crisis, rising Treasury yields near 5.1%, an 85%-priced-in December Fed hike, and Iran-related geopolitical risk. QQQ is already down 5.6% over the month and trading below its 50-day MA, suggesting momentum is negative into a risk-heavy week with NVDA earnings on Nov 17.
picks.news: US markets fell Nov 12 on Nvidia CEO exit, Iran tensions, and Fed hike expectations with Nasdaq -0.39%; futures only modestly higher Nov 13 ahead of PPI data (2026-11-13).
picks.risks: A benign PPI print or dovish Fed signals could spark a relief rally; this is a low-conviction, broad macro hedge rather than a company-specific view, and QQQ's mega-cap diversification (MSFT, AAPL, AMZN) limits pure NVDA contagion.
